newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway's Statoil improves Q1 result.
newsitem.headline: Norway's Statoil improves Q1 result.

text.p: State Norwegian oil company Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) said on Thursday first-quarter income after tax rose by 200 million crowns ($28.2 million) to 1.4 billion thanks to higher oil prices.
Operating profits for the Statoil group increased to 5.2 billion crowns from 4.0 billion in the first quarter of 1996.
Overall revenues for the period came to 30.2 billion crowns, up from 24.3 billion for January-March last year.
"This increase primarily reflects higher oil prices," the company said in a statement.
"The average price of Brent reference crude during the first quarter was $21.20 (140 crowns) per barrel, as against $18.60 (119 crowns) in the same period of 1996," it said.
But equity crude production declined to an average of 426,000 barrels per day (bpd) from 445,000 bpd in the same period last year.
"This contraction largely reflects difficult weather conditions off Norway in early 1997," Statoil said.

The company had to curb production several times at the North Sea fields Statfjord, Gullfaks and Snorre because of stormy weather. The maximum permitted wave height for shuttle tankers to moor at offshore loading buoys is 4.5 metres.
But the Statoil-developed submerged turret loading (STL) system on the Heidrun field off mid-Norway helped to maintain production despite these problems, the company said.
"No significant changes in the level of production are expected during the second quarter by comparison with the first quarter," the statement said.
"Assuming relatively stable prices for the group's principal products, profits for the second quarter are expected to be slightly lower than in the first three months," it said.
Daily sales of equity gas averaged 21.7 million cubic metres, up from 19.6 million.
Two new contracts covering natural gas deliveries to Italy and the Czech Republic respectively were concluded during the first quarter.
First-quarter operating profits for the petrochemicals business totalled 97 million crowns, an improvement of 99 million from the same period of last year.

"This increase reflects better margins for polyethylene and polypropylene. Regular production from the methanol plant at Tjeldbergodden in mid-Norway will start during May, about two months later than planned," it said.
The company's Status Weekly newsletter said Statoil achieved the best operating profit per barrel produced among the world's 100 leading oil and gas companies.
This ranking was done by auditors Price Waterhouse and Petroleum Intelligence Weekly, it said.
